name: Navigation API
plain: Gives a single place to listen to and control same-document navigations.
meaning: A single page app can intercept link clicks and back or forward, and list its own history entries. It sees only same-origin entries, so it cannot read browsing history.

access.persistence: Entries live in the tab session
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

limits.headline: Can watch and control page changes inside the app, such as when you press Back
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you click links, press Back, or move around the app.
can: Notice when you click a link or press Back inside the site
Update the page without a full reload
Hold up a page change until a save finishes
cannot: Watch what you do on other sites or in other tabs
Block you from leaving the site
Change the address to another site's address
See where you came from outside its own pages

story.what_it_is: A modern way for a page to manage its own links and Back button handling.

marketing.name: Navigation API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say the API modernizes single page app routing with one clear set of tools.

story.for_you: You never see it. When it works, apps feel snappier and Back and Forward behave more predictably inside big web apps.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to build cleaner routing than the older history tricks, with animation hooks and a proper list of past entries. It is mostly a developer quality and speed win.

use_cases.example: A web mail app changes folders without reloading and keeps Back working.
A streaming site slides between pages with an animation while loading the next view.
A store keeps your scroll position when you press Back from a product.
A framework wires its router to the API so one place handles every in page link.
A measurement script catches every in page navigation without brittle hacks.
A live blog moves between match pages without breaking the real time feed.

technical_bounds: entries() lists only same-origin entries of the current tab
The same back button hijack mitigations apply (entries without user activation are skippable)
Cannot read other tabs or other origins' history
Support per MDN BCD: Chrome 102, Safari 26.2, Firefox 147
